overview.en: This West African hairstreak is one of two recognized species in the small genus Dapidodigma.
overview.fr: Ce thécla ouest-africain est l’une des deux espèces reconnues du petit genre Dapidodigma.

identification.en: Males have a pale hindwing patch centered on the cell; in D. demeter it lies above.
identification.fr: Chez les mâles, la tache pâle de l’aile postérieure est centrée sur la cellule ; chez D. demeter, elle est au-dessus.

habitat.en: Recorded in forest, dry forest and scrub, often associated with Alchornea.
habitat.fr: Signalé en forêt, forêt sèche et broussailles, souvent associé à Alchornea.

diet.en: Its larval food plant is unknown.

behavior.en: Females were found among plants attended by Oecophylla ants.
behavior.fr: Des femelles ont été trouvées parmi des plantes fréquentées par des fourmis Oecophylla.

reproduction.en: Larvae and pupae of Dapidodigma are attended by ants.
reproduction.fr: Les larves et les pupes de Dapidodigma sont accompagnées par des fourmis.

ecology.en: Unlike forest-only D. demeter, it also occurs in dry forest and scrub; see its profile.
ecology.fr: Contrairement à D. demeter, limité à la forêt, il vit aussi en forêt sèche et broussailles ; voir sa fiche.

conservation.en: No global conservation assessment was located in the sources reviewed.
conservation.fr: Aucune évaluation mondiale de conservation n’a été localisée dans les sources examinées.

title.fr: Genre Dapidodigma Karsch — Metamorphosis, Société des lépidoptéristes d’Afrique

facts: Specialist review of markings, habitat and host records.

title.fr: Dapidodigma — Tree of Life Web Project

facts: The synopsis recognizes two species in the genus and reports ant attendance of larvae and pupae.

facts: The nomenclatural bibliography lists both Dapidodigma species and the taxonomy used in historical literature.

uncertainties: No larval host has been established; Alchornea is described as an association, not a confirmed food plant.
No global conservation assessment was located in the consulted sources.
review_note: Used the specialist genus review for species comparison, habitat and host knowledge; Tree of Life and FUNET are genus and nomenclature cross-checks. D. demeter is linked reciprocally; no degraded-habitat use or larval feeding on Alchornea is inferred.
